proposal_title: Formal Addition of GenerationJob.attempt_index and 90-Minute Safety Lease TTL
domain_specific_rationale: From the Flow Browser Specialist (R06) perspective, CP-018 provides crucial guarantees for browser-based generative AI workflows. Browser automation with third-party providers like Google Flow involves inherent latency characteristics: jobs frequently experience external provider queuing delays, complex multi-pass diffusion generation cycles (5-15 minutes), and multi-gigabyte media asset downloads. Setting the safety lease TTL to 90 minutes with 30-second worker heartbeats provides the browser worker runtime sufficient runway to complete end-to-end execution without risking premature lease revocation or duplicate task assignment by the R02 reconciliation engine. Furthermore, adding attempt_index (integer >= 1) to GenerationJob enables precise attempt-scoped idempotency key derivation (job_id:attempt_index), preventing browser retry attempts from colliding with prior failed or interrupted browser sessions. This eliminates race conditions during browser crash recovery and retry dispatch.
capability_impact: Directly preserves CAP-01 (Canonical Core State Integrity), CAP-02 (Google Flow Adapter Execution), and CAP-04 (Workflow Engine Orchestration) by ensuring robust execution lease protection and deterministic retry isolation for long-running browser worker automation.
residual_risk: If an unresponsive browser worker fails to heartbeat while retaining an active lease, the 90-minute safety lease TTL creates an extended recovery window before automated reconciliation occurs. Mitigated by R09 worker-side watchdog timers that abort stuck Playwright contexts upon element/page interaction timeouts (30s/10s) and explicitly release leases or report terminal errors.
